name: Tractian
description: Tractian is privately held and has no ticker. Review its funding rounds and valuations, the investors and SPVs that hold its shares, and the points to confirm before buying or selling.
ledes: Tractian is a privately held industrial technology company. Its shares are not listed on an exchange and have no quoted market price; the principal public reference points are the valuations at which the company has raised capital. Its most recent financing, a $130 million Series D round announced on October 22, 2026, valued the company at $1.4 billion.

Founded in 2019 and based in Atlanta, Tractian sells sensors and AI software that track the condition of machinery in factories and other industrial sites, so that maintenance teams can address faults before equipment breaks down. Existing shares change hands in privately negotiated transactions, frequently through special purpose vehicles, and remain subject to the company's transfer restrictions.
figs: Special purpose vehicles with SEC filings naming Tractian
table_note: Valuations are as announced by the company. Tractian did not disclose a valuation for its Series B or Series C.
round_notes: Sapphire Ventures led the Series D, with M&G's Catalyst as co-lead. With the Series D announcement, Tractian said that more than 2,000 customers worldwide use its platform; that figure is the company's own.

A round valuation reflects the terms of the preferred stock issued in that round. Most shares sold by employees are common stock, which carries fewer rights and typically trades at a discount to the preferred price.
investors: Sapphire Ventures led the Series D, with M&G's Catalyst as co-lead, and also led the Series C. General Catalyst led the Series B. Other investors include Next47, NGP Capital, Bosch Ventures, Monashees, Endeavor Catalyst and Y Combinator.
spv_sentence: Three special purpose vehicles formed to invest in Tractian have filed with the SEC, all of them in 2026.
sources: Sources: Tractian's announcements of its Series D (October 22, 2026), Series C (December 5, 2024) and Series B (August 7, 2023); and SEC Form D filings.
